_comment: Building specs: markets, mills, prestige buildings, mitigation infrastructure. Filled in during Phase 2.
_guildsNote: Phase 21.6 (D2, docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-03-phase19d-economy-depth-design.md), deviating from that spec in three ways. (1) upkeepSurchargeFraction replaces a flat upkeepSurcharge: the doc's own numbers were broken against THIS file's incomePerYear (cloth 1.40/200 nets exactly zero on a market; iron 1.35/180 is strictly worse) because a flat surcharge silently changes ratio the moment incomePerYear is retuned. A fraction reduces the 'no guild ever worse' rule to one static check per type — incomeMultiplier - 1 > upkeepSurchargeFraction — that cannot rot. (2) charterFee (new field, not in the doc) makes 'grant' cost something: without it, granting with an empty treasury is a free way to dodge the refusal unrest spike, which BACKLOG/PLAN.md flags as an exploit. resolveGuildPetition() downgrades an unaffordable grant to a refusal. (3) guildPetitionBaseChance and guildRefusalRepetitionWeight are dropped entirely — nextGuildPetition() is a pure function of state with ZERO new RNG draws (the single most valuable property in the design: it keeps the shared seeded stream byte-identical with every other change in this phase), so there is no roll to weight. petitionMinRank is 0-indexed against data/ranks.json (Baron=0): cloth/iron unlock at Baron so specialization is visible from turn one (bug report #51's 'monotonous, specialization not visible'); salt at Duke(1), wine at Prince(2) per the plan's explicit deviation from the doc's flat Count/Prince gating, chosen because those are the ranks a 60-year game actually reaches — see data/ranks.json's own _populationNote on why Count and above are rarely reached inside 60 years. guildRefusalCooldownYears keeps a refused type from being re-offered next turn without an RNG-weighted roll.

tradingHouse._note: Unlocked at Count (rank 3, see data/ranks.json unlockedFeature). Was Margrave (4) until the D2 commerce calibration — Merchant/Raider typically plateau near Count with high treasury and low population, so a Margrave-gated unlock meant the Commerce alt path for ranks 5-7 was unreachable for the archetypes it was meant to serve. Income is sized so a single trading house roughly breaks even against the wealth-proportional tribute (economy.json upkeep.tradingHouseTributePercentage) at typical mid-game treasuries, then falls behind as wealth grows — the anti-snowball shape every other late-game building follows.

cathedral._note: Tied to Archbishop Prestige-path populationMin in data/ranks.json (2600) — the first rank that requires cathedral:true. Was 5000 (B1, unreachable), then 2800 (still above Archbishop's stated threshold — B5). Keep this equal to (or below) that rank's populationMin whenever ranks are recalibrated.

dike._note: F6: flood's dedicated mitigation building — deliberately NOT shared with well/drought, so a ruler on flood-prone (wet-weather) exposure faces a real, separate investment rather than one building covering both ends of the weather distribution for free.
